label: Explanation of presence at a moment: a primitive relation of a reason to a thing's presence
term: explains a thing's presence at a moment (Lean `PresenceExplanation.Explains`)
definition: PresenceExplanation.Explains v r x t: in history v, the reason r explains x's being present at moment t. A reason is any explanans token, causal or not: a giver, an earlier state together with a law, a necessity. Explicitly identified PRIMITIVE relation; no axiom constrains it, and nothing ties it to BeingGiving.GivesAt (definition 158301bc) except the explicit open productive bridge (ExplanationNeedsGiver). Ordinary meaning: the explanans of 'why is S there at m?', as in Schmid's deduction of S's existence at m from its earlier existence, the absence of any inducer of its cessation and the causal law on change, or in an explanation that cites a sustaining cause. Distinguished from giving being at a moment (an exercise of causation of being, agent side), from tenseless causing of being (CausesIn ... esse), from grounding, and from the world-indexed explanation of an existence fact in the existence-PSR models (TruthCore.Explanation.ExistencePSR.Model.explains, no moment).
note: Analyst primitive, attribution deferred, introduced to type the momentary principle of sufficient reason that Schmid 2021 (read; passage SCHMID-INERTIA-REPLY-3-ARTICLE, paragraph beginning 'And this discovery especially helps') accepts from Feser's argument. Structural properties: none built in (not functional, several reasons for one presence are allowed, no closure under composition, no factivity: soundness, that an explained presence obtains, is not assumed). OPEN: which explanans types are adequate; Schmid's origin-or-inertia explanation (definition 8c20c988) is one defined sense. Would be sourced by a passage stating a time-indexed explanatory principle for existence, which the Schmid passage does in prose only.
